findings.title: Truth's arrival and falsehood's instability

findings.mechanism: The focus al-haqq is joined to the commanded saying and to 17:80's request for truthful entry, truthful exit, and supporting authority; the closing witness and failed production demands later in the pericope place that declaration under public examination. Al-batil is paired with zahaqa and zahuqan, and 17:82 makes the consequence concrete by describing healing for believers and increased loss for wrongdoers.
findings.reader_payoff: Arrival and disappearance become more than two equal events: one pole is publicly named and answerable, while the other cannot hold a stable place.
findings.containment: This does not claim that the focus noun itself means to prove, or that a truth-agent causatively invalidates an object. The causative b-t-l branch is excluded because its argument structure does not fit the actual carrier. The later test and witness are contextual readings, not a verdict on the arguments themselves.

epistemic.reason: The channel nomination is supported by supplied focus forms and neighboring context, but the synthesis across the pericope remains an interpretive relation.

findings.title: A carrier fitted to its recipients
findings.claim: 17:94-95 changes the focus arrival from content alone to a delivered message whose carrier fits its recipients: people object that guidance came through a human messenger, and the counterfactual answers that settled earth-dwelling angels would receive an angelic messenger.
findings.mechanism: The focus al-haqq and ja'a meet the 17:94 arrival of guidance and the human-messenger objection, then 17:95's matched earth-walker and angel-messenger pair. The focus word's joint/receptacle facets supply a bounded analogy for a carrier correctly fitted to its place.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the messenger's humanity as part of the delivery relation, not a defect separate from the truth that arrives.
findings.containment: The joint/receptacle reading is an analogy from two exact facets of the supplied B011 record; al-haqq is not being redefined as a joint or vessel. The counterfactual answers this local objection and does not establish a universal formula for every revelation.

epistemic.reason: The HFT roots and context coordinates match the supplied Arabic; the fit from lexical image to messenger-recipient relation remains attributed.

findings.title: A declaration under witness
findings.claim: The closing witness turns the focus statement from an assertion resting on its own force into a public claim held between disputing parties under testimony, inner knowledge, and sight.
findings.mechanism: The focus al-haqq, as a binding object of the declaration, meets 17:96's sufficient witness between speaker and audience, followed by the statements that God knows and sees inwardly. The witness supplies the separate verification relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The line's force becomes answerable testimony rather than self-certification by the speaker.
findings.containment: The HFT's live alternative remains: 17:96 may settle messenger credibility rather than adjudicate the full truth/falsehood mechanism. The excluded q-w-l title branch does not fit the focus imperative qul.

epistemic.reason: The witness, sufficiency, knowledge, and sight occurrences align with the supplied context; their return to the focus is attributed.

findings.title: A trajectory that reaches or overshoots
findings.claim: With 17:84's guidance and path beside it, the focus can also be pictured as two trajectories: truth penetrates its proper target, while falsehood expends motion past the target and disappears.
findings.mechanism: The focus haqq carrier meets the supplied straight-penetration facet; zahaqa and zahuqan meet the target-overshooting facet; 17:84's guidance and traversable path provide the independent spatial field.
findings.reader_payoff: Truth and falsehood become unlike movements, one reaching its place and one missing by passing beyond it, rather than only static opposed contents.
findings.containment: This is the packet's exploratory branch-driven spatial analogy, not an archery scene in the ayah. It leaves the ordinary truth and disappearance readings intact and does not claim that the focus literally names a weapon or path.

epistemic.reason: The two focus facets are registered and the 17:84 word coordinates match, but the trajectory synthesis is explicitly exploratory and analogical.

One branch identity conflicts internally: the entrusted-presence trace's q-l-l at 17:85 word 14 matches قَلِيلًا, but root_001251/B001 is paired in the registry with q-w-l and focus occurrence قُلْ. The branch is excluded while the exact 17:85 surface remains contextual evidence.

Context carrier/trigger arrays therefore use the supplied ayah member ref, and the descriptive field pins the traced word index.
